title: Jira story to executable Playwright-BDD automation
description: Orchestrator-driven, spec-driven workflow with three mandatory human approval gates. Every stage is idempotent and resumable from durable workflow state.

batching.note: Never process all stories or all tests in a single model invocation. Capability, tag, risk and release are also supported batch axes.

entryPoints.description: Default. A story that has never been processed.
A story whose approved requirements are unchanged but whose tests must change - most commonly adding API coverage to an already-automated story. Re-enters at Gate 2 and passes Gates 2 and 3 only.
rules: Gate 1 is NOT re-run. The acceptance criteria are unchanged and already approved; re-approving them wastes a reviewer and risks producing a divergent AC set for one story.
Only stages whose inputs are provably unchanged may be skipped. Compare the approved requirement artifactVersion against the one the previous run recorded; if it moved, use NEW_STORY instead.

Reuse the existing instance WF-<JIRA-ID>-R<release> and reset it. There is deliberately one instance per story and release, so a second instance for the same pair cannot exist: the workflowId is derived from jiraStoryId and release and is rejected if it disagrees with them. Do NOT invent a release that Jira does not have in order to get a second instance - that release would then leak into the RTM and into feature tags.

Resetting an instance does overwrite it, so the evidence of the previous run must be preserved elsewhere BEFORE the reset: append a WORKFLOW_RESTARTED event to workflow/history/<workflowId>.history.jsonl, which is append-only, and confirm the prior state is committed to version control. If either is missing, stop - the protection this rule exists for is gone.
Existing execution records, approvals and defect artifacts are historical evidence and are never regenerated or overwritten.
The revised test plan is a new artifactVersion of the same TEST-PLAN-ID, merged by testScenarioId. Existing scenarios are preserved; new scenarios are added.
An added API scenario must not retire a UI scenario covering the same acceptance criterion unless a human explicitly approves the retirement at Gate 2.

stages.blockedWhen: Atlassian MCP authentication is unavailable or the deployment is Jira Server/Data Center.

rules: Preserve every extracted AC verbatim in originalText.
Every proposed AC requires a rationale supported by available Jira context.
Unsupported information is recorded as REVIEW_REQUIRED, never invented.

stages.invokes: Existing OpenSpec skills and prompts (opsx-propose / openspec-propose). Never fabricate OpenSpec filenames or conventions.
rules: Only APPROVE-d acceptance criteria may be used.
OpenSpec artifacts describe business behaviour only - no selectors, locators, page objects, fixtures or TypeScript.
Every scenario declares an interfaceType. Absence means UI, so a plan written before API support stays valid.
Whether an acceptance criterion is API-verifiable is a testing judgement, not a stated requirement. Propose it with a rationale and mark it REVIEW_REQUIRED; never decide it silently.
An API scenario may ADD coverage. It may never REPLACE a UI scenario - that would delete the only end-to-end proof of a journey while leaving the coverage number unchanged.
An API or HYBRID scenario must carry an apiContract. Never guess an endpoint, a field name or a status code.
The review package lists every proposed contract so the human approving Gate 2 is agreeing to it explicitly.
This gate is where an OBSERVED contract becomes HUMAN_APPROVED. A human agreeing to the endpoint, status codes and response shape is exactly as authoritative as an OpenAPI document.

An approved plan may not assert an acceptance criterion against an OBSERVED or UNVERIFIED contract. Observed traffic records what the application does, not what it should do, so it would make a current bug the definition of correct.
Explore approved scenarios only.
Never add unapproved business requirements.
Record application-versus-specification mismatches instead of silently changing an approved expectation.
Replace MCP_VALIDATION_REQUIRED placeholders only with validated locators.

Discover API contracts by driving the approved UI flow and recording the calls the application really makes (browser_network_requests). Never guess an endpoint - a guessed DELETE has side effects a guessed locator does not.

Observed traffic is recorded with contractSource OBSERVED. It is evidence of what the application does, never authority for what it should do, and it cannot back an assertion until Gate 2 approves it.
Replace API_CONTRACT_UNVERIFIED placeholders only with a contract that has real provenance.

stages.blockedWhen: PLAYWRIGHT_BASE_URL, credentials, application access or test data are unavailable. Record BLOCKED - never fabricate a passing result.

rules: Evidence is copied out of test-results/ before anything else; the next run overwrites it.

ENVIRONMENT_BLOCKER outranks every other signal. DNS, TLS, proxy, refused connection or missing configuration means the application was never reached, so the failure proves nothing about it. Halt - never heal it, never file it.
Classification is mechanical. AMBIGUOUS is routed to healing first, because an unnecessary heal is cheaper than a false bug.

Read the failing scenario's @interface- tag BEFORE classifying. An API scenario exercises no locator, so LOCATOR_SUSPECT and AMBIGUOUS-routed-to-healing do not apply to it - routing one to the healer would burn both attempts against a DOM the test never touched and then file a locator bug it never was.

An API failure is CONTRACT_MISMATCH when the call completed but violated the approved contract, APPLICATION_DEFECT when the behaviour itself is wrong, and ENVIRONMENT_BLOCKER when the request never reached the application. A 502, a refused connection or a TLS failure is a blocker; a 401 is only a blocker when the test never obtained a credential at all.
An API-only failure has no screenshot. Its evidence is the redacted request/response exchange, recorded in evidence.apiExchanges. Never record an empty evidence set instead.
expectedBehaviour is the approved acceptance criterion verbatim. Never paraphrase it and never invent one.
A fingerprint that already belongs to a REPORTED defect is recorded as DUPLICATE, not filed again.
stages.blockedWhen: reports/execution/results.json is absent or the failing test carries no @ac- tag, so the failure cannot be traced to an approved acceptance criterion.

rules: Only locators and waits inside src/pages/** and src/components/** may change.
Feature files, step definitions, assertions and test data are out of bounds - changing them would change the approved behaviour under test.
test.fixme, test.skip and waitForTimeout are forbidden. Silencing a test is not healing it.
After two attempts without a green re-run, set classification LOCATOR_UNHEALABLE and outcome NOT_HEALED, revert speculative edits and hand over to BUG_REPORTING.
An APPLICATION_DEFECT never enters this stage.
An @interface-api scenario never enters this stage. It exercises no locator, and src/api/** is outside the blast radius. Refuse and hand back, exactly as for an ENVIRONMENT_BLOCKER.
A CONTRACT_MISMATCH never enters this stage. Either the application changed or the agreed contract is wrong, and both are human decisions rather than something a test may absorb.
stages.blockedWhen: The scenario cannot be re-run, so no attempt can be evidenced.

rules: fixVersions are read verbatim from the story under test. If the story has none, BLOCK - never guess a release.
The bug is linked to the story and assigned to the configured reviewer. An unassigned bug is an unreviewed bug.
Severity, priority and root cause are never invented. Raise them as open questions in the description instead.
The agent proposes the RTM defectRefs update; only the orchestrator merges it.
stages.blockedWhen: JIRA_BUG_ASSIGNEE_ACCOUNT_ID is unset, the story has no fixVersions, or the Atlassian MCP session is not authenticated.

stages.invokes: Existing OpenSpec skills (openspec-archive-change, or openspec-sync-specs when the change stays open). Never hand-edit openspec/specs/.
rules: Close the change opened at OPENSPEC_GENERATION. Without this the change list grows forever and openspec/specs/ never becomes the source of truth.
Archive only after the RTM records real execution evidence. Archiving a change whose scenarios never ran would file an unproven spec as delivered.
A change with deferred acceptance criteria is archived only for the criteria that were delivered. The deferred ones stay visible as open work; never silently drop them.
The CLI is the only writer. Run `npx openspec archive <change-name>` and let it move the files.
stages.blockedWhen: `openspec validate <change-name> --strict` fails, or the RTM shows no passing execution for the story.

mergeProtocol: Delegated output is written to an isolated *.proposed.json file.
The orchestrator validates the proposed update.
The orchestrator acquires a processing lock covering the target traceability files.
The orchestrator validates the merged artifact.
The orchestrator appends the update to workflow/history/<workflowId>.history.jsonl.
idempotencyChecks: Does the output artifact already exist?
Did the source artifact version change?
Is another workflow instance processing it?
Did the previous stage complete successfully?
Is the current stage allowed to execute?
Are all required approvals recorded in validated workspace artifacts?
Does a defect with this failure fingerprint already exist, and was it already REPORTED?
Has the two-attempt locator healing cap already been reached for this defect?

failurePolicy.schemaValidation: Attempt exactly one correction, then stop and report the exact blocker.
